en: The Bloodline of the Master-Disciple Succession Entrusted by Preceptor Xuan of the Ci’en Monastery in the Left Ward of Chang’an City, on the seventeenth day of the eighth month of the sixth year of the Xiántóng era of the Great Táng, spanning both the Fetal and Golden Realms.
Mahāvairocana and Vajrapāṇi of the Garbhadhātu Realm.
Dharmagupta Shenvuwei (entrusted to three persons),
Xuanchao (entrusted to one person).
Huiguo (who transmitted it to six persons):
Weishang and Bianhong.
Eiheiji, Kōkai, Gimon.
Yi Cao (entrusted with six people);
Fa Run and Fa Quan (entrusted with eight people).
Xuánzàng composed this himself; Tányǒu completed it with his wisdom.
Ennin (and those who followed from Japan):

Enchin and Enzai (Enzai traveled to Tang China on the same ship as Great Master Jikaku; while he was receiving the Dharma from Hōzen alongside Chishō Daishi, his term of office expired and he returned to the court, where he suddenly encountered a violent storm at sea and perished, it is said).
Pianming Zongrui Yizhen (The Universal Illumination of the Profound Meaning of the True Doctrine)
Profoundly penetrating the great encounter of the ocean-like clouds.
Wen Yuan (one lineage), Vajrabodhi.
Vairocana of the Vajradhātu and Samantabhadra.
Mañjuśrī, Nāgārjuna, and Āryadeva.
Vajrabodhi (three individuals), Śubhakarasiṃha,
and Amoghavajra (the *Jingangding yijue* states that in the seventh year of the Kaiyuan era, Master Amoghavajra arrived at the Western Capital and requested the precepts and empowerment).
Wu Kong (five people),
Han Guang,
Yuan Jiao.
Huilang (1 person); Tianzhu (3 persons);
Layman Zhao Zheng (4 persons).
Yi Guan Zhi Qing Shan Zhen (The Meaning of Abundant Water: Pure Will and Virtuous Integrity)
The Imperial Edict on the Fundamental Wisdom and Reverent Cultivation of Virtue (for one person).
Yaxiao, Tanzhen,
and Juechao.
Huide Qiurui Huiguo (Ten persons)
Wisdom is the fundamental governance that arises from the convergence of conditions.
Zao Xuan Yuan Ren Wen Wu (The Profound, Perfect, Benevolent, and Enlightened)
May grace and response be ever esteemed; may the days of grace continue.
The meaning of the vast ocean of emptiness is fully realized through eloquent exposition.
Gyōmyō, Giei, and Gyōsō (thirteen persons).
*Hōun-gi-shin-gi-jū* (or,
as some say, *E-kwa-bō-dōji-chi-shō-daishi-sei-un-gi-jū*; so it is said).
Giyū (when the Great Master entered Tang China, he personally visited that *ho-shang*, etc.);
Shin-tatsu (a person from Tōji says it was *Hōzen ho-shang*, etc.); Kaun.
Daiyu follows He Wen to the garden.
Junliang (Jun: jūn; liang: liàng; jun also read as jūn; meaning level, equal, and universal; liang means trust, mutual, and assistance).
Changjianfaguan (entrust to six persons).
Hongyue Ziyu and Yuanzhen.
Encompassing All and Universally Illuminating: The Essential Wisdom of the School.
Wen Bi (Literary Secret)
